_comment: Single source of truth for the value-equity-investor skill. Edit this file to change behavior. Set enabled=false to pause all autonomous equity trading without deleting the schedule.
_history: Created 2026-08-16 when the user switched the Agentic account's primary strategy away from short-dated options (see trading/config.json) to long-term value-equity investing, after a rough first week of options trading (-27% in week 1).

risk_limits.notes: max_new_trades_per_day=20 is a user-specified ceiling, not a target -- this is a slow-accumulation strategy and will rarely place more than a handful of buys in one run. max_position_pct_of_account=15% and the target_position_count below (in entry policy) together drive per-trade sizing toward roughly even diversification across 8-12 holdings. cash_reserve_usd is a small buffer left unspent to absorb price moves between screening and fill.

instrument_scope.notes: Long equity positions only, bought with dollar-denominated fractional-share market orders in regular_hours. No options, no shorting, no margin. This skill NEVER sells -- see exit policy below.

screening.note_on_percentage_filters: The scanner's PERCENTAGE-unit filters (net profit margin, ROE, etc.) take fractional values, not whole percentage points -- 8% is '0.08', not '8'. Confirmed by testing: passing '8' silently returns zero results instead of erroring.

qualitative_judgment.notes: The quantitative scan produces a shortlist, not a buy list. Before buying, apply judgment on top of it: (1) check get_financials (a few recent quarters, revenue and net income) for a business that is stable or growing, not visibly deteriorating despite a cheap headline multiple -- that combination is the classic value-trap pattern; (2) favor well-known, easily understood businesses over thinly-traded or structurally complex names for this account's size; (3) prefer US-domiciled, standard common stock -- be cautious with foreign ADRs (VIE structures, delisting/regulatory risk) and highly cyclical commodity/shipping names, which the scan's low-P/E ranking tends to surface disproportionately since cheap multiples are often structural in those sectors, not a mispricing; (4) diversify across GICS-ish sectors -- avoid ending up with several picks that are all the same sector because they dominate the bottom of the P/E ranking (financials/insurance/energy naturally cluster there); (5) skip a statistically-cheap name if get_financials shows a clear multi-quarter decline in revenue or margin -- note the skip and reason in the log rather than forcing a fill of target_position_count.

entry.sizing: Each run: room = min(risk_limits.max_position_pct_of_account * current_account_value, (cash_available - risk_limits.cash_reserve_usd) / max(1, slots_remaining_to_target_position_count)). Skip a candidate if room < risk_limits.min_new_position_usd. Place as a dollar_amount market order in regular_hours (fractional shares).

exit.notes: This skill only ever buys. It never places a sell order on an equity position, regardless of price move, valuation change, or any other signal. If a position needs to be sold, that is a decision only the user makes, executed manually or by explicit one-off instruction outside this skill's autonomous run. Do not add a stop-loss, profit-target, rebalancing-sell, or any other autonomous sell trigger to this skill without the user explicitly asking for one.

order_execution.notes: Dollar-based fractional orders only execute in regular_hours; if run while markets are closed the order queues for the next regular open.
